grades.quote: When a file’s reference count reaches zero, fileclose releases the underlying pipe or inode, according to the type.
grades.reason: Provides indirect lifetime-management context, but these reference counts belong to open-file objects, not inodes.

grades.quote: iput() doesn’t truncate a file immediately when the link count for the file drops to zero, because some process might still hold a reference to the inode in memory
grades.reason: Explains how inode references preserve lifetime while processes still use the file, but does not explain inode locking.

grades.quote: The file’s inode and the disk space holding its content are only freed when the file’s link count is zero and no file descriptors refer to it.
grades.reason: Explains the ownership/lifetime side: descriptors keep an unlinked inode alive. Exclusive locking is not discussed.

grades.quote: Freeing an object that is protected by a lock embedded in the object is a delicate business, since owning the lock is not enough to guarantee that freeing would be correct. The problem case arises when some other thread is waiting in acquire to use the object; freeing the object implicitly frees the embedded lock, which will cause the waiting thread to malfunction. One solution is to track how many references to the object exist, so that it is only freed when the last reference disappears.
grades.reason: Directly explains the separation: exclusive locking alone cannot ensure object lifetime, whereas reference counts prevent freeing an object that others still reference.
